title: Turning Interaction History into Execution State: A Runtime Layer for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
summary: Ledger replaces the model's implicit inference of execution status from raw interaction history with a deterministic runtime layer that injects a compact state view into each prompt (inform) and intercepts commands to replay still-valid results or flag redundant work (govern), wrapping an unmodified agent. It costs no additional language-model calls and only the engineering effort of maintaining the ledger and its command-interception logic, with reported net cost reductions. It can fail when the ledger's staleness tracking misclassifies state, causing the govern path to return cached results that no longer reflect the repository or to suppress legitimately needed re-execution, and gains may not transfer to agent frameworks or task distributions unlike those evaluated.
rationale: The layer is model-agnostic, adds no inference calls, reduces API spend, and improves resolution on a standard benchmark, making it directly deployable within a single-GPU or API-only budget.
technique: Deterministic execution-state ledger for coding agents

It can fail when the ledger's staleness tracking misclassifies state, causing the govern path to return cached results that no longer reflect the repository or to suppress legitimately needed re-execution, and gains may not transfer to agent frameworks or task distributions unlike those evaluated.

Pass@1 rises from 56.2% to 64.2% with GPT-5 mini and from 75.8% to 81.0% with MiniMax M2.5 on SWE-bench Verified, while total cost falls 28.9% and 31.8% respectively; attached to OpenAI Codex it adds 3.4 Pass@1 points at 24.4% lower cost.
